title: Alvarado Score
sources: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986;15(5):557-564

changelog.change: Added an explicit pediatric cross-reference (PAS / pARC in the Peds Module) as a notes line; expanded the source citation.
Initial entry — the adult-derived score. For children use PAS or pARC in the Peds Module.

purpose: Bedside probability of acute appendicitis in adults; supports the imaging / surgical-consult decision. Adult-derived — for pediatric patients use PAS or pARC instead.

items.label: Migration of pain to the RLQ

interpretation.label: Appendicitis unlikely
interpretation.disposition: Observation and serial exams; imaging if suspicion persists

interpretation.label: Equivocal
interpretation.disposition: Imaging (CT in adults) or a period of observation

interpretation.label: High probability
interpretation.disposition: Surgical consultation; imaging often still obtained to confirm

notes: Adult-derived (Alvarado 1986). For children, use the Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS) — or, in a child ≥ 5 years with < 96 h of pain where an absolute neutrophil count is available, the Pediatric Appendicitis Risk Calculator (pARC), which is more decision-actionable. Both are in the Peds Module under Pediatric Appendicitis Score, which also compares all three tools. Alvarado is weighted heavily toward WBC and performs best at the score extremes, less so in the equivocal 5-6 range.
